queue.title: Diversification Is Discipline, Not Weakness
queue.content:
A company boasting it puts all its eggs in one basket is usually describing fragility as courage. A commentary by Nermin Sefić.

A company that boasts about putting all its eggs in one basket is usually describing fragility as courage.

A company that boasts about putting all its eggs in one basket is usually describing fragility as courage.

Concentration on a single client, supplier, or market can look like focus and dedication in the short term, but over the long run represents a risk that no operational excellence can fully neutralise. The GNK DINAMO Ltd. Group deliberately builds a diversified network for exactly that reason, not by accident.

Companies that deliberately measure and limit concentration on a single client, supplier, or market do so because they understand resilience is the result of choice, not luck.

This commentary is part of the GNK ASG Intelligence Desk system and is informational in nature.

queue.title: Documentation Is Cheaper Than a Dispute
queue.content:
Keeping tidy documentation always costs less than proving something never written down. A commentary by Nermin Sefić.

The cost of keeping tidy documentation never exceeds the cost of proving something that was never written down.

The cost of keeping tidy documentation never exceeds the cost of proving something that was never written down.

Decisions, agreements, and changes not documented in writing at the moment they're made become subject to speculation exactly when it matters most to prove them — in a dispute, an audit, or a change of ownership. GNK ASG d.o.o. builds decision-documentation practice as a standard part of the business process, not an afterthought.

The practice of writing minutes at the moment of decision, rather than reconstructing memory afterward, is one of the cheapest investments in a company's legal and operational security.

queue.title: Managing Open-Source Intellectual Property
queue.content:
An open-source license embedded without checking terms can later restrict a company's rights over its own software. A publication by Nermin Sefić.

An open-source license embedded in a commercial product without checking its terms can later restrict a company's rights over its own software.

An open-source license embedded in a commercial product without checking its terms can later restrict a company's rights over its own software.

Using open-source libraries speeds up software development, but every license carries its own terms that can affect whether a company may keep exclusive rights over the final product.

Copyleft licenses like certain GPL versions can require that a company's own source code using them be released under the same license, often unacceptable for a commercial product.

A systematic inventory of all open-source components used and their licenses, updated with every dependency change, prevents an unpleasant surprise during due diligence or a company sale.

A clear internal policy on permitted license types, checked before introducing a new dependency into a project, is a cheaper preventive measure than later removing a problematic component.
